target: workflow.sh merge — unusual project content (trailing spaces, blank lines, unicode, a decoy line that looks like a marker but uses the wrong prefix) survives a merge byte-for-byte
cmd: source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/workflow.sh"; source "$FIXTURES/workflow-fixture.sh"; wf_file project.js '// unmarked line with trailing spaces:   ' '' '<!-- @agentic-loop:begin region=decoy -->' 'unicode: héllo wörld 日本語 🎉' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("PLACEHOLDER");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=notes owner=project' 'these are my project notes, do not touch   ' '// @agentic-loop:end region=notes' '' '// trailing file comment'; wf_file template.js '// unmarked line with trailing spaces:   ' '' '<!-- @agentic-loop:begin region=decoy -->' 'unicode: héllo wörld 日本語 🎉' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("REPLACED");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=notes owner=project' 'ignored upstream notes text' '// @agentic-loop:end region=notes' '' '// trailing file comment'; wf_file expected.js '// unmarked line with trailing spaces:   ' '' '<!-- @agentic-loop:begin region=decoy -->' 'unicode: héllo wörld 日本語 🎉' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=greet owner=plugin' 'console.log("REPLACED");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=greet' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=notes owner=project' 'these are my project notes, do not touch   ' '// @agentic-loop:end region=notes' '' '// trailing file comment'; VERDICT=$(workflow_merge project.js template.js '//' '{}'); MATCH=$(cmp -s project.js expected.js && echo true || echo false); jq -n --argjson v "$VERDICT" --argjson m "$MATCH" '{verdict:$v, match:$m}'
_note: expected.js is hand-built with the exact same wf_file primitive as project.js, differing only in the refreshed region's body, so cmp -s is a true byte-exact assertion — not a substring check that could hide truncated whitespace, dropped blank lines, or mangled unicode. The HTML-style decoy marker line (right syntax, wrong comment prefix) guards against the scanner false-positiving on text that merely mentions a marker.
